name: POST /api/deliverability/address/verify - Can this address receive mail at all
description: Answers whether an address is REACHABLE: syntax, reserved/placeholder/disposable policy, and whether the domain publishes a mail exchanger. This is a different question from POST /api/deliverability/check, which asks whether a recipient is SUPPRESSED. It runs the same functions as the gateway's pre-send guard, so a portal verdict and a send cannot disagree. Body: address (string) or addresses (string[], at most 100), recheck? (skip the cache for a single address). It is not tenant-scoped, since an MX record is a fact about DNS rather than a tenant, but it needs a Bearer token because it performs outbound DNS on caller input. 200 { data: { results[] (input, address, domain, verdict, code, reason, checks, mail_exchangers, allowed, blocked_because), checked, deliverable, undeliverable, risky, unknown, would_block, policy } }. A bad address is a 200 with verdict undeliverable, not a 400. Errors: no address, or more than 100, 400; no token 401.

testCases.name: A malformed address is a 200 verdict, not a 400 (no DNS needed)
Batch: one verdict per address supplied
